subject: OmniPay call — capacity & latency options
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@omnipay.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + follow-ups from today (capacity & latency)

Hi Samira — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size a pilot and draft a short SOW:

- Goals you articulated: real-time UX calls (chat/completions) with p95 latency target around 200ms for short completions (~<150 tokens), and background batch workloads (offline enrichment) with higher latency tolerance.
- Traffic shape: baseline ~300 qps with expected marketing-driven spikes up to ~900 qps for short windows (10–30 minutes).
- Security/data residency: SOC 2 required; EU data residency for some EU customers (you noted).

Options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest path to production, regional routing, autoscale for spikes — good if you accept variable cost and want to avoid infra ops.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput and cost; better for sustained high QPS and tighter p95 SLAs.
- Private VPC/on-prem: for strict residency/compliance needs and air-gapped environments — longer lead time.

As next steps, could you please: (1) share a small sample of representative payloads (1–2MB of requests, anonymized) and (2) confirm whether the 200ms p95 applies to all chat types or only UI micro-interactions? I attached a short pilot spreadsheet that outlines the metrics we typically collect.

Attachments: omnipay-pilot-qps-sla.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

I'll loop Rafael in to provide a preliminary capacity estimate based on the sample payloads once you share them. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up next week to lock the pilot window.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samira Khan <samira@omnipay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: OmniPay Procurement <procurement@omnipay.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + follow-ups from today (capacity & latency)

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 200ms p95 target applies to UX micro-interactions only (card-authorize style prompts), which are ~40–120 tokens. Longer generative flows (documentation, long-form replies) are OK up to ~1s p95.
- Traffic: baseline 300 qps is accurate. Spikes historically reach ~600–900 qps, but those are transient (10–20 minutes). Planning horizon is Q4 ramp — procurement is evaluating committed capacity vs variable spend.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II proof is required; EU residency applies only to customer-facing data (we can route EU users to EU regions).

We'll prepare a payload sample (anonymized) and send by Monday. Procurement would like a pricing ballpark for (a) hosted with burst support and (b) dedicated reserved capacity for steady 500 qps with 2x burst headroom.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, OmniPay
samira@omnipay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@omnipay.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + follow-ups from today (capacity & latency)

Hi all — quick technical note that I captured for the pilot and commercial framing. High level numbers (very rough):

- For short completions (~100 tokens, p95 target 200ms): with our optimized serving runtime and continuous batching, a single A100-class equivalence (or M60 x N on public clouds) can sustain ~150–200 qps at p95 ~200–250ms for GPT-sized models (fp16 / int8 depending on quantization).
- To cover a sustained 500 qps baseline with 2x burst headroom (peak ~1000 qps), plan for ~3 dedicated GPUs (sized as above) plus autoscale/burst nodes. This assumes prefix caching for repeated prompts and KV reuse; without caching the numbers increase ~30–40%.
- Hosted path: autoscaling groups + short warm-up may handle spikes, but predictable p95 at 200ms under 900 qps spikes is easier with Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Private VPC: similar capacity needs; additional lead time for networking and KMS.

Attachments: capacity-estimate-omnipay.pdf (est. compute breakdown)

I'll prepare a short table comparing cost-per-qps estimates for hosted vs dedicated (back-of-envelope). Monica — I'll drop the table and a short runbook into the pilot doc link.

—Rafael
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
